name: DecoNFlow RRBS-CL tumour-fraction limit of detection
description: Median limit of detection of the tumour fraction for reference-based deconvolution tools on the RRBS-CL mixtures.

attributes.protocol: Build a reference of tumour and healthy cfDNA samples, select the top 250 hypomethylated DMRs per entity (adjusted p < 0.01) with each of limma, DMRfinder and wgbstools, deconvolve every mixture with each tool, then compute the limit of detection per combination. Lowest tumour fraction at which the estimated fractions of the ten replicates are significantly higher than those of 0% tumour samples (one-tailed unpaired Mann-Whitney U test, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p < 0.01), moving from higher to lower fractions; tested grid 0.0001, 0.001, 0.003, 0.007, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5.
attributes.version: Preprint version 1, Methods 'Evaluation metrics and missing values'; DecoNFlow v2.2.0
attributes.unit_detail: Tumour DNA fraction of the mixture (0.007 means 0.7%)
attributes.aggregation: Median over the combinations analysed (tumour types and DMR selection tools); the pooled combinations are not listed in the table
limitations: In silico mixtures, not patient plasma.
Values are medians on a discrete grid of tested fractions; medians can fall between grid points.
The table does not state which combinations each median pools.
Preprint, not peer reviewed.
attributes.source_locator: Preprint Methods 'Evaluation metrics and missing values' (pages 26-27) and Figure 4 legend; Supplementary Table 3

name: SPOT-MAS five-class tissue of origin, discovery cohort 10-fold cross-validation
description: Tissue-of-origin accuracy within the discovery cohort.

attributes.protocol: Classify each cancer patient's plasma into one of five cancer types (breast, colorectal, gastric, liver, lung) from nine concatenated SPOT-MAS feature sets; report the proportion of patients assigned to the correct type, overall and per cancer type and stage. Discovery cohort, 10-fold cross-validation.
attributes.version: eLife 12:RP89083, Methods 'Construction of models for TOO'
limitations: Cancer patients only; no healthy or other-cancer samples are classified, so false localisations in non-cancer plasma are not measured.
Features combine methylation with fragment length, copy number and end-motif signals; not a methylation-only workflow.
Author-reported by the assay developer (Gene Solutions); no independent replication.

Table S9 breast and all-cancer stage strata use different stage counts from Tables S1, S2 and S8 and article Table 1; those 24 results per protocol are disputed. All-stage values and the other cancers' stage strata are unaffected.
attributes.source_locator: Article Methods 'Construction of models for TOO' (P49-P53); Supplementary file 1 Table S9 rows 2-10

name: SPOT-MAS five-class tissue of origin, independent validation cohort
description: Tissue-of-origin accuracy of the discovery-trained models on the validation cohort.

attributes.protocol: Classify each cancer patient's plasma into one of five cancer types (breast, colorectal, gastric, liver, lung) from nine concatenated SPOT-MAS feature sets; report the proportion of patients assigned to the correct type, overall and per cancer type and stage. Models trained on the discovery cohort, applied once to the validation cohort.
attributes.version: eLife 12:RP89083, Methods 'Construction of models for TOO'
limitations: Cancer patients only; no healthy or other-cancer samples are classified, so false localisations in non-cancer plasma are not measured.
Features combine methylation with fragment length, copy number and end-motif signals; not a methylation-only workflow.
Author-reported by the assay developer (Gene Solutions); no independent replication.

Table S9 breast and all-cancer stage strata use different stage counts from Tables S1, S2 and S8 and article Table 1; those 24 results per protocol are disputed. All-stage values and the other cancers' stage strata are unaffected.

The GCNN was trained transductively on a graph that includes the validation-cohort samples as nodes (Methods P51), so its validation accuracy is not from a model that never saw the validation features. RF and DNN were trained on the discovery cohort only.
attributes.source_locator: Article Methods 'Construction of models for TOO' (P49-P53); Supplementary file 1 Table S9 rows 11-19

name: Sun et al. 2024 five-cancer detection from deconvolved plasma cfMethyl-Seq (ROC-AUC per cancer type)
description: Real-world disease detection test in Sun et al. 2024, cfMethyl-Seq cohort; one AUC per cancer type against the same healthy group.

attributes.protocol: Deconvolve each plasma sample against a full 35-cell-type reference atlas with each method, then train a random forest on the estimated cell-type fractions to separate patients from healthy individuals and report ROC-AUC. One comparison per cancer type against the 193 healthy individuals.
attributes.version: Sun et al. 2024, Methods 'Assessment of deconvolution performance on real-world datasets' (P49)
limitations: The random forest training and evaluation split (cross-validation or held-out) is not stated; the AUC may be in-sample.
Discrimination AUC, not sensitivity at a declared specificity.
No uncertainty is reported for the AUC values.

metric_implementation.note: Random forest settings and resampling not stated

attributes.source_locator: Article P30 (cohorts), P49 (AUC definition); Additional file 1 Table S7 rows 5-9
